text:
The MGAP National forest cartography (version 2021), from Uruguay's Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries, is the source that classifies the loss area by forest type. It maps about 13.1 ha of the 13.5 ha loss area as native forest. About 0.4 ha falls outside mapped forest, and none is planted forest.

The other two sources don't make that distinction. Hansen GFC measures the loss (13.5 ha, 3.91% of the asset). JRC GFC2020 only confirms forest was present in 2020 over 98% of the event area, and it includes plantations.

The MGAP map gives territorial context, not cause. The evidence doesn't establish that deforestation happened, why, or whether it was legal. The 2025 loss is also still pending corroboration, because no later year has been observed.
